segments.text: HItherto we haue spoken of the commandements of the first table: nowe followeth the secōd table, which concerneth the loue of our neighbour. Rom. 13.9. Thou shalt not commit adulterie, thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not steale, thou shalt not beare false witnes, thou shalt not couet: and if there be any other commandement, it is briefly comprehēded in this saying, namely, thou shalt loue thy neighbour as thy selfe.
Our neighbour is euery one, which is of our owne flesh. Esa. 58.7. When thou seest the naked couer him, and hide not thy selfe from thine owne flesh.
The manner of louing is so to loue our neighbour as our selues, to witte, truly and sincerely: when as contrarily, the true manner of louiug God, is to loue God without measure.
The second table containeth sixe Commandements: whereof the first, &, in the order of the ten commandements, the fift, concerneth the preseruation of dignity and excellencie of our neighbour.
Honour thy Father and thy mother, that they may prolong thy daies in the lande, which the Lord thy God giueth thee.
